title: Kirandeep Kaur, 24-Year-Old Indian Mother, Stabbed to Death in London Home While Sleeping Beside Newborn
excerpt: A man broke into the family home in Hayes and allegedly attacked Kaur as she lay in bed with her husband and baby. British police have charged Daniel Sean James with murder.
body:
A 24-year-old Indian woman was stabbed to death inside her home in London in a horrifying attack that has left the Indian diaspora community in shock.

## What Happened

Kirandeep Kaur was allegedly stabbed in the chest while she slept beside her husband and their newborn baby at their home in Hayes, West London, in the early hours of Sunday, July 13. According to prosecutors, the attacker — a stranger — had broken into the family's home through a window after reportedly stabbing another man outside on the street.

Prosecutors told a British court on Thursday that Kaur screamed after being stabbed, waking her husband, who saw a figure escaping through the bedroom window in the darkness. Despite the efforts of paramedics from the London Ambulance Service, Kaur was pronounced dead at the scene.

The accused, Daniel Sean James, 46, allegedly broke both ankles after jumping from the bedroom window. Police arrested him outside the home and charged him with murder, attempted murder, and possession of a bladed article. The man stabbed outside the home, in his 20s, was hospitalized with injuries described as not life-threatening.

## A Family Shattered

Kaur had moved to the United Kingdom from Punjab's Tarn Taran district nearly two years ago on a student visa. Her father, Sukhdev Singh, told Indian media that the family had sold agricultural land to finance her higher education in the UK, hoping she would build a secure future abroad. After completing her studies, she had obtained a work permit and begun working in England.

Her brother-in-law told the Metro newspaper that she was "a wonderful mother" who had just had a baby. "The family were so happy. We are heartbroken," he said. A family friend described her as "a really lovely person" and said the family is devastated.

## Court Proceedings and Community Response

James appeared before Willesden Magistrates' Court and was remanded in custody. The London court has set dates for the murder trial to proceed.

Kaur's brother, Gurvinder Singh, told reporters that the accused had allegedly attacked another man before entering their home while trying to evade police. Investigators are examining the exact sequence of events and the motive behind the attack. The family has characterized the killing as a hate crime, though police have not confirmed this classification.

Detective Chief Inspector Allam Bhangoo of the Metropolitan Police called it "a shocking incident which has tragically resulted in one woman losing her life."

The case has reignited concerns about the safety of Indian nationals in the UK, particularly among young professionals and students who have moved abroad in search of better opportunities.

*Sources: People Magazine, The Sun, Dainik Jagran English, Metropolitan Police*
author: Diaspora Desk
